title: PRD: Tenant-weighted SLO tiers and burst-protection circuit playbook for conversational routing
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Define a product-level SLO and rollout playbook that (1) assigns tenant-weighted latency and availability tiers, (2) implements an automated burst-protection circuit breaker that preserves high-priority tenants during platform-wide overload, and (3) specifies measurable acceptance criteria + observability hooks required for safe progressive rollout.
background: We operate a multi-tenant hosted inference stack where a small number of large tenants and many smaller tenants share capacity. Recent edge incidents showed tail-latency and cache-thrashing events where low-priority background workloads consumed capacity during bursts, degrading service for high-priority tenants. Existing SLOs are global and do not reflect tenant importance or protect against transient overloaded windows. This initiative creates explicit tenant-weighted SLO tiers and an automated burst-circuit that enforces graceful degradation and model-fallback routing to protect higher tiers.
metrics: Primary metrics to define and monitor: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end generation latency (first-token and per-token streaming where applicable), request success rate (2xx), request error rate (5xx/4xx), per-tenant error budget consumption, queueing latency, GPU utilization per pool, KV cache hit ratio, and circuit-triggered re-routes. Derived metrics: weighted-burn-rate (tenant priority weight applied to error budget consumption), degradation-impact-score (measure of quality loss when routed to fallback model).
acceptance_criteria: SLO tiers defined and documented: Tier-1 (critical): p95 first-token <= 120ms, availability >= 99.95%; Tier-2 (standard): p95 first-token <= 250ms, availability >= 99.9%; Tier-3 (background): best-effort with availability >= 99.5 and backlog-friendly routing.
Error budget model implemented that computes per-tenant and aggregate burn with tenant weights and exposes a dashboard for the last 1h/24h/7d windows.

Automated burst-protection circuit logic implemented in routing plane: when cluster-weighted burn-rate > 1.5x over 5m and queueing latency increases > 2x baseline, the circuit engages and applies the configured actions (priority shaping, spillover to Dedicated or lower-cost model variants, rate-limits background tenants).
Canary rollout passes defined safety gates for 1%, 10%, and 25% traffic rings with concrete thresholds (see rollout_plan).
Observability: dashboards for p99 tail, weighted-burn-rate, per-tenant cache-hit ratio, and circuit activations; alerts wired to on-call with runbook links.

Automated rollback triggers defined and validated in canary: if weighted-burn-rate exceeds 2.0x baseline for 10m or p99 latency increases > 30% for Tier-1 tenants, rollout is automatically halted and previous routing rules reinstated.
Runbook and communication templates exist for customer-facing incidents when the circuit engages and a Tier-1 tenant experiences degradation.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dry-run against synthetic traffic in staging; validate metric collection and circuit simulation. Phase 1 (Canary 1%): rollout routing changes to 1% of production traffic (non-critical tenants only). Observe for 48h; gate to Phase 2 if no safety gate violations. Phase 2 (Canary 10%): include a mix of Tier-2 tenants; run 72h; validate burn-rate, p99, and cache behavior. Phase 3 (25%): expand to additional regions and enable priority shaping for a small set of Tier-1 test tenants under active monitoring. Phase 4 (Global): enable for all host clusters with automated rollback monitors and per-tenant overrides. Each phase has automated stop gates and a human approval step before phase increase.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create a new SLO dashboard with weighted-burn-rate, per-tenant SLO status, circuit state timeline, and model-fallback counts. Alerts: Sev-P0 alert to SRE and on-call PM if Tier-1 p99 > threshold or weighted-burn-rate > 2x baseline for 10m. Alert to product and SE if circuit triggers more than 3 times in 24h. Integrate with slack channel #platform-slos and create a high-priority PagerDuty schedule for initial rollout window.
rollback_criteria: Immediate automated rollback if any of: (1) Tier-1 p99 latency increase > 30% sustained for 10m, (2) weighted error-budget burn-rate > 2.0x baseline for 10m, (3) unhandled 5xx rate for Tier-1 tenants > 0.5% for 5m. Manual rollback if localized regions show degraded availability > 0.5% for 30m. All rollbacks must be logged with root-cause hypothesis and next-action owned by on-call.
